threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'brolly' instead of an umbrella and wonder why no one else does. Welcome to London!
Caught a bloke singing opera on the 35 last night—turns out he’s a barista at that café down Coldharbour Lane. Who knew?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I realized I was really home was when I saw a man arguing passionately with a pigeon over a piece of bread outside the kiosk on Hermannstraße.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop open at 3 AM, serving spicy vegan versions alongside traditional meat ones, all with a side of techno beats.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they’ve got a favorite taco truck and can name the best late-night burrito spot without hesitation.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy get off the 31, wearing a full tuxedo, and just started dancing on the corner. Only in San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Many tourists think they can just order a 'café' and get espresso. Here, 'café amb llet' is the real go-to for a morning pick-me-up.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a new arrival by their bewilderment at the local baker's closing hours. They still think croissants are a morning item, not a late afternoon treat.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still avoid walking on the cracks in the pavement. The locals are already dodging dog doodle like pros.
Caught a night bus from Brixton last week, and an old chap serenaded the driver with a ragged rendition of 'My Way'—made the whole ride feel like a film.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I heard a toddler speaking fluent Turkish while an old man on his balcony yelled at pigeons—it felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find spontaneous street art festivals that seem to pop up overnight, turning blank walls into vibrant canvases. It's like a citywide gallery opening every weekend.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they know the secret ways to dodge the BART delays and still make it to Dolores Park before sunset.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 31 heading down Eddy, and a guy serenaded us with an old Aretha song. Everyone forgot the delays and just smiled. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about the parks and squares, but the real vibe is in the way locals swap recipes over morning coffee at tiny bakeries.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they mispronounce 'Gràcia'—it's not 'Graa-sia', it's 'Grat-sia'. That little slip gives them away.
